text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel wants to raise VAT by one percentage point
- A survey showed that 50 percent of Czechs welcome the Czech-German reconciliation accord to be signed in Prague today
- Deutsche Telekom plans further acquisitions abroad
- German car production rose in 1996
- Opposition Social Democrats expects 4.5 million unemployed
- Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt opposed to full taxation of share earnings
HANDELSBLATT
- German shares closer on record high
- Deutsche Telekom exceeds expectations in turnover and results for 1996. Shareholders can expect a dividend of 60 pfennigs even though they have only held the shares for 44 days
- Waigel wants to raise VAT to 16 percent
- The supervisory board of troubled engineering group Deutsche Babcock dismisses board chairman Heyo Schmiedeknecht. Klaus Lederer will take his place
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Bonn plans tough penalties for child-sex offenders. Therapy for sex felons should be obligatory
- Government commission on income reform wants to lower top corporate tax rate to 35 percent from 47 percent and the highest rate for individuals to 39 percent from 53 percent
- Number of car thefts drops by 15 percent
- Head of Grundig , Pieter van der Wal resigns
- More firms are being set up in west Germany than in east Germany, perhaps a sign of halting east German economic growth
- Rexrodt rejects plans for full taxation of shares
DIE WELT
- Waigel remains the target of heavy criticism. He defends his tax reform plans
- The left wing of the Social Democrats, in contrast to party leader Oskar Lafontaine, in favour of coalition with the environmentalist Greens
- Image of German army improved among population at large
- Price war over passengers. Deutsche BA attacks Lufthansa
- Good figures give Telekom shares a boost
- Social Democrats says there is no impulse to create jobs in Bonn's proposed tax reform
